page_title: Evaluating where your team lies on the SRE spectrum | Google Cloud Blog

sources.entry: Are we there yet? Thoughts on assessing an SRE team’s maturity

summary.name: Evaluating where your team lies on the SRE spectrum
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud blog post by Customer Reliability Engineer Alex Bramley that offers four principles and self-assessment questions for judging whether an operations team is practicing Site Reliability Engineering.
use_cases: Assessing whether an ops team qualifies as an SRE team
Deciding how SREs should engage with development teams
Setting up SLO and error budget feedback loops
Planning incident response and postmortem practices
Reducing repetitive operational load through automation
Explaining SRE principles to an organization
summary.what_it_does: The article examines the question "can we call ourselves SREs yet?" by separating three meanings of "SRE": a job role, a group of people, and a set of principles. It proposes four principles: SREs mitigate present and future incidents, actively regulate service reliability using SLOs and error budgets, engage early and comprehensively in design, and automate repetitive work. Each principle comes with self-check questions. The post also gives a counter-example of a consulting SRE team in an advisory role, where development teams hold responsibility for reliability. It is an opinion piece, not a formal framework or scoring system.
notable: Four principles with concrete self-assessment questions for SRE teams
Covers consulting or advisory SRE models as well as directly engaged teams
Separates the SRE job role, team, and practice definitions
Written by a Google Cloud Customer Reliability Engineer
caveats: Explicitly not an authoritative answer; it gives opinions and rough consensus, not pin-point accuracy
Principles assume teams that directly support production services; indirect teams may need to adapt them
